title: Temporal Score Rescaling for Temperature Sampling in Diffusion and Flow Models
claim: A single inference-time rescaling knob steers sampling sharpness or flatness and improves outputs across many different generative tasks.
layout: 4 panels in 2x2 grid; baseline vs ours columns, colored sharper/flatter labels
description: The figure is a 2x2 grid of four task panels, each comparing a baseline sampler with the same sampler plus TSR (temporal score rescaling). Top-left, Mixture of Gaussians: three heatmaps of probability density evolving over time, with 1D marginal density curves at the sides. They are labeled DDPM, +TSR sharper and +TSR flatter. The sharper version gives peaked marginals and the flatter version gives broader ones. Top-right, Pose Prediction: an input image of a pyramid-like object, and two Mollweide spherical projections with colored pose-sample clusters. These are labeled Score Sampling and +TSR sharper, and the sharper version has tighter clusters. Bottom-left, Depth Estimation: an aerial photo of a Ferris wheel, then DDIM and +TSR sharper depth maps. Bottom-right, Image Generation: a text prompt and two photos of a man in sunglasses, labeled Flow-ODE and +TSR flatter. The sharper labels are orange italic and the flatter labels are teal italic.
caption: Temporal Score Rescaling (\ours) provides a mechanism to steer the sampling diversity of diffusion and flow models at inference. Top-left: Probability density evolution when sampling a 1D Gaussian mixture with DDPM, and the effects of \ours , which can control the sampling process to yield sharper or flatter distributions. Top-right, bottom: \ours can be applied to any pre-trained diffusion or flow model, improving performance across diverse domains such as pose prediction, depth estimation, and image generation.
abstract: We present a mechanism to steer the sampling diversity of denoising diffusion and flow matching models, allowing users to sample from a sharper or broader distribution than the training distribution. We build on the observation that these models leverage (learned) score functions of noisy data distributions for sampling and show that rescaling these allows one to effectively control a 'local' sampling temperature. Notably, this approach does not require any finetuning or alterations to training strategy, and can be applied to any off-the-shelf model and is compatible with both deterministic and stochastic samplers. We first validate our framework on toy 2D data, and then demonstrate its application for diffusion models trained across five disparate tasks -- image generation, pose estimation, depth prediction, robot manipulation, and protein design. We find that across these tasks, our approach allows sampling from sharper (or flatter) distributions, yielding performance gains e.g., depth prediction models benefit from sampling more likely depth estimates, whereas image generation models perform better when sampling a slightly flatter distribution.
